approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a score-ranked population using crossover and local edits, retains the best scored survivors, and learns from every accepted observation in the current session. Its fixed count-fingerprint Gaussian process supplies correlated function draws over each fresh pool. Each draw buys its highest available candidate; after three batches without a new incumbent, eligibility narrows to the forty highest predicted means. Canonical identity checks and the sulfur gate constrain the same graph proposal process.
approach.novelty: Replace the single predictive function law with an evidence-weighted mixture of three complete Gaussian processes: the original count Tanimoto model, exact min/max count overlap, and normalized-count Matérn. All three see every accepted record; each sampled function uses one expert chosen according to its current archive evidence. This preserves uncertainty about which complete model to trust. Earlier fixed substitutions committed every purchase to one alternative, a learned descriptor blend selected one covariance, and a regime mixture partitioned records then compressed predictions into a Gaussian. Current-host siblings changed preference likelihood, count information, allocation or graph-search control; none used this whole-model mixture. The new claim is that the mixture will make exposed paid departures with better ordering, which may produce larger real gains.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is weak conversion of continued local search into additional endpoint progress, while the current predictor commits every function draw to one fixed covariance. On code Parent n-cf8d309c06de the complete Search mean is 0.607030316211131 (population seed SD 0.030175277546149237); read-only reconstruction of its actual 4350 purchases gives full incumbent gain 5.978073077532332 but only 1.0224077547621127 in the late 2175 purchases, with 88 of 435 batches restricted. This is not evidence that all remaining limitations are ranking errors: its purchased strict-pair ordering earns 13773/19495 correct credit, and proposal/retention limitations remain. The historical fixed min/max n-dd2b25d32925 and normalized Matérn n-ea03f38e7e10 had fully exposed changed selections yet lost 0.04824526182151967 and 0.02750824038854201 against their actual old Parent n-62daf219c70a; each ordered its own purchased labels worse than the same-state original GP. The learned descriptor covariance blend n-5cc22bb8f56b improved purchased ranking yet lost endpoints; n-0142fbe4db04 improved MSE yet lost 0.047786449523025666. The partitioned moment-matched regime mixture n-1c27fae8e61d was scientifically refuted and lost about 0.136643; its membership/precision weighting is not a retained capability. Current-host sparse probit n-aaeb1a1ac082 converged in 435 fits but worsened purchased ordering in every cell and lost 0.101371920532155. Current count and crossover removals n-b5a14afe9b35 and n-060debe936b2 lost 0.05414999595897533 and 0.051489597325333016, supporting preservation of these capabilities conditionally. The frozen whole-model mixture is therefore a distinct testable uncertainty/ordering hypothesis, not a positive replication of failed kernels. Sources and per-cell reconstruction are recorded in policy/scratch/r0062-02-improve-L01/evidence-review.json and its audit-seed files, alongside the original Search logs and trajectories.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent supplies exact finite-pool conditioning, accepted labels and a joint sampler. No unpurchased labels are required.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Finite-model uncertainty with evidence weights and one categorical expert per complete sampled function.

deviations.adopted_setting: Exact finite-pool conditioning, fixed historical kernels, shared empirical score normalization, full-archive refits and retained stall mask.
deviations.paper_setting: Random-feature paths, continuous optimization and periodic hyperparameter fitting.
deviations.reason: These are frozen ticket constraints. No approximation or convergence guarantee is transferred.

adoptions.implementation_change: FingerprintPosterior.fit computes archive evidence weights; select draws an expert per original normal row, then its exact conditional GP function.

literature_review.conclusion: The primary-source construction makes this frozen intervention implementable. Internal negative results require separating model exposure, paid ordering and full progress; they do not establish useful mixture behavior. Review supports one discriminating test, not automatic continuation.
queries: Direct reread of frozen primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2205.14090v2 sections3 and3-B; no new search query or new literature source.

sources.applicability: Use the frozen three full-archive molecular GPs and inherited mask. The source establishes the construction, not molecular ranking or endpoint benefit.
sources.finding: Equations7–10 define a finite GP probability mixture, evidence weights, and categorical-model then conditional-function sampling; section3-B repeats this law for synchronous batches.
sources.title: Lu et al., Surrogate modeling for Bayesian optimization beyond a single Gaussian process, v2

method_change.previous_method: One exact accepted-raw-score count-dot-Tanimoto GP supplies all joint function rows on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de.
method_change.proposed_method: Exact evidence-weighted probability mixture of the three frozen full-archive GP models, one categorical expert per entire conditional function row.
method_change.rationale: The frozen ticket addresses whole-model uncertainty after exposed fixed substitutions, fitted covariance blending and partitioned moment matching failed. The molecular generation/population host remains inherited. Its full conditional factors, normal stream and accepted archive already support the required coherent component replacement; neither a complete-method replacement nor a second intervention is necessary.

hypothesis: One component replacement on n-cf8d309c06de: model identity is a global latent variable for each complete GP function, with fixed dictionary order [original_count_dot_tanimoto, exact_count_minmax_tanimoto, normalized_count_matern32]. Every expert conditions on the same full chronological accepted archive and the same raw-score transform z=(y-mean(y))/max(population_SD(y),0.001). For expert m, factor A_m=K_m(X,X)+0.05^2 I+j_train,m I using the original float64 ladder and compute ell_m=-0.5*||solve(L_m,z)||^2-sum(log(diag(L_m)))-0.5*n*log(2*pi). With fixed prior probabilities 1/3, logw_m=ell_m-log(3)-logsumexp_k(ell_k-log(3)). Recompute from the complete current archive each fit; never multiply repeated full-archive evidences. Conditional raw mean mu_m=mean(y)+scale*K_m(X,Q)^T*A_m^-1*z and standardized latent covariance C_m=K_m(Q,Q)-V_m^T V_m use that expert coherently in every block. The mask mean is mu_mix=sum_m w_m*mu_m. For each inherited normal row Z_r, independently draw one model M_r from categorical(w) on an isolated session stream, and construct the entire raw function row mu_Mr+scale*Z_r*chol(C_Mr+j_pool,Mr I)^T. Apply the inherited sequential availability and first-index maximum rule with the same K=3/M=40 stall predicate; no within-batch conditioning is added. This exact finite mixture is generally non-Gaussian: neither kernels nor function rows are averaged, no maximum-evidence expert is selected deterministically, no record partition or per-candidate expert is used, and no moment-matched Gaussian is sampled. Shared empirical normalization makes these empirical-normalized evidence weights conditional on the transform, not fully Bayesian inference over a learned normalization. The causal prediction is non-original expert exposure -> changed paid identities and same-label ordering -> accepted feedback and potential larger progress.

finding_summary.headline: Mixture sampling changed purchases, but ordering worsened and endpoint value fell
finding_summary.insights: The borrowed finite-model sampling construction worked, including real alternative-expert exposure and delivery of its labels into later learning and breeding. Its promised ordering repair failed on the registered complete-panel test. Better mean squared error and predictive log density did not translate into better ranking or larger total progress, and extra late progress did not recover the early loss. Evidence weights often concentrated strongly: 163 of 435 fits had a numerically exact maximum weight of one, and average entropy fell from 0.285 in early purchases to 0.019 in the late third. This establishes a limitation of the tested evidence-weighted mixture, without isolating a harmful expert or proving that ranking alone caused the endpoint loss. The method still searches mainly around earlier molecules: after excluding tiny fragments, median nearest-prior count-fingerprint similarity was 0.918, rising to 0.923 late, versus 0.910 and 0.915 for the Parent. The molecular assessment finds related leader families, tied peripheral variants, reactive heteroatom bonds and strained fused systems; the Child also bought 150 molecules with at least fifty heavy atoms versus 46 for the Parent, while tiny-fragment counts were 85 versus 98. These observations support examining ranking models or proposal/search schemes that distinguish useful core and connectivity changes and preserve coherent structures. They do not establish a universal size rule, a diversity-collapse cause, or a chemically justified automatic rejection rule. The result settles this registered mixture’s ordering and full-progress predictions on the frozen panel; broader mixture methods, component attribution and causal mediation remain open. GPU factors and RNG states were recorded as hashes, so exact cross-platform byte reconstruction remains an audit limit, despite successful numeric replay of all logged consequences and whole-function samples.
finding_summary.results: All 435 three-expert fits ran successfully. Non-original experts supplied 2,613 of 4,350 purchases; 988 purchased molecules were outside the original GP’s passive selected sets, and 1,281 choices were strict departures under the same eligibility mask. Every changed record with a later opportunity reached the next fit and probe. Yet the mixture correctly ordered 13,534 of 19,414 unequal-label pairs (69.7126%), compared with 13,611 (70.1092%) for the original GP on exactly the same purchased labels. Ordering worsened in 11 of 15 task/seed cells and improved in four, triggering the registered ordering falsifier. Full incumbent gain fell from 5.97807 to 5.17520, although late-half gain rose from 1.02241 to 1.30318. Mean final score fell from 0.607030 to 0.553505 (delta −0.053525); all three seed means fell, with five task/seed endpoint gains and ten losses. Seed dispersion was similar (population SD 0.02985 versus 0.03018), and the protocol’s paired task-safety rule flagged the sitagliptin task. The unchanged +0.002 endpoint criterion was not met.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain amines and carbonyls, but reactive heteroatom bonds and strained fusions persist near score peaks
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-a1818ac8ff05 against code Parent n-cf8d309c06de uses the frozen Search panel only: seeds 0/1/2, all five tasks, 300 recorded observations per task and seed, including 10 initial records and 290 optimizer proposals. Both child_complete and paired_complete are true; all 15 Child staging trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were read, with no missing paths or missing task comparisons. No Confirmation evidence was read. The Child remains in staging; no future archive path is assumed. Byte-identical staging snapshots, original paths and hashes are recorded in policy/scratch/r0062-02-improve-L01/molecular/input-manifest.json, alongside separate audit-seed-N-task.json files. The final trajectory row is the last evaluated candidate, not necessarily the incumbent. Initial molecules are starting context, not generator output. The digest reports ring-closure rates from 0.9736 to 0.9874 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.9701 to 0.9839 across the five sets of 870 proposals; these are SMILES-text presence rates, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. RDKit structure perception of the recorded proposals gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 37, 35, 32 and 27 in the frozen task order. The structures are predominantly substituted polycycles, heteroaromatics, aryl amides or thioamides, N-rich carbonyl heterocycles and halogenated amine/aryl assemblies. They show real ring and functional-group variety, with seed-specific analogue families; there is no general absence of basic amine-like centres or aromatic rings. All 4,350 Child proposals parse, as do the matched Parent proposals. Nevertheless, Child counts include 546 molecules with N-halogen bonds, 241 with O-halogen bonds, 248 with O-O bonds and 37 with acyl halides; the corresponding Parent counts are 888, 162, 118 and 8. These overlapping graph flags are liabilities to inspect, not measured instability, toxicity or synthesis scores. There are 85 Child proposals with at most six heavy atoms and 150 with at least fifty, compared with 98 and 46 for the Parent. Both tiny fragments and elaborate fused/bridged structures recur. Digest charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 for every task, while structure perception finds unassigned tetrahedral stereocentres in 2,417 Child proposals. Neutral notation does not mean absence of ionisable nitrogen. Moderate structural diversity reflects substantial whole-panel variation but related leaders within sessions; it does not imply a proven diversity deficit causes scores. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are qualitative readings: many ordinary motifs occur inside structures with reactive bonds, steric congestion or unresolved geometry. No synthesis, conformational feasibility, protonation or experimental activity was measured. All comparisons below are molecular-score associations under this panel, not activation decisions, causal component contributions, or claims that a particular missing group is an objective requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are predominantly indole-like aryl carboxamides or thioamides with alkyl, methoxy, halogen and pyridyl/anilide substituents. The median size is 25 heavy atoms and the observed range is 1 to 48. Seed 0 develops a compact but densely bridged cage with an N-hydroxy pyridyl carboxamide; seed 1 keeps a substituted indole/pyridyl carboxamide with N-O substitution; seed 2 retains a fused indole/thioamide family. The underlying amide and heteroaryl chemistry is familiar, but unusual ring closures and N-O, N-S or N-halogen substitutions make several leaders questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: Bridged and four-membered ring motifs, N-hydroxy/N-sulfenyl amides, and N-halogen substitutions occur in scored families; nearby scores do not establish their stability or makeability.
The final thioamide family includes N-brominated heterocycles, while oversized coupled aromatic structures and bare fragments occupy the low-score tail.
missing_features: The seed-2 leading thioamide family lacks the pyridyl carboxamide environment seen in the higher Child seeds; this is a conditional structural association, not proof that the group itself explains the difference.

A consistently less strained, stereochemically defined implementation of the compact aromatic/carboxamide arrangement is not demonstrated. More ring count alone is not the missing capability: the best Child cage already has seven perceived rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child maxima in seed order are 0.4692371322034651, 0.42956033293511225 and 0.3747076276871866. The seed-0 N-hydroxy cage leads an otherwise related NH-carboxamide cage scoring 0.43109245871924246, while two seed-1 compounds differing by aryl Br/F tie at 0.42956033293511225. This supports a local topology/polar-group association, not a universal benefit from extra halogenation. A 45-heavy-atom coupled aromatic amide/thiourea structure scores 3.315183114286997e-17, and the tiny disulfane scores 0.0: neither enlarging nor stripping the scaffold is generally productive here. Published Parent maxima are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554; its leaders are mostly less bridged indole amides, but also include N-halogen chemistry. The Child changes the leading topology, with mixed seed comparisons. Its seed-2 last thioamide scores 0.24981617138296136, below that seed incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic output set: median 37 heavy atoms, range 1 to 118, with fused heteroaryl carbonyl systems and long unsaturated appendages. Seed 0 develops N-rich fused lactam/imide-like structures carrying cyclic cumulenes; seed 1 gives densely fused aza-aromatic cyclic carbamate-like systems with a three-membered sulfur bridge and a chlorinated alkyl substituent; seed 2 concentrates on linked heteroaromatics bearing peroxide/acetal and diene groups. Ordinary heteroaryl/carbonyl fragments are embedded in highly elaborate topologies whose synthetic plausibility is questionable. The digest cumulated-double-bond rate is 0.1425.
liabilities: Peroxide motifs occur in 194 of 870 proposals, and cyclic cumulenes, long conjugated chains and an unsaturated three-membered sulfur ring complicate stability and synthesis.
Large highly fused or repeated assemblies increase topological complexity without a consistent score gain; even the Parent leader is not a chemically clean reference.
missing_features: The Child seed-0 branch does not reproduce the compact polar fused-ring arrangement associated with the substantially higher Parent seed-0 score; its elaborated cumulene structures are a different chemical solution.

Seed-2 leaders lack the cyclic carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement of the higher Child seed-1 family. The trajectories do not identify a universal missing decoration or prove that removing peroxide or reducing size would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All three seeds start with a best score of 0.548381482770623. Child maxima are 0.6082968398627057, 0.6365303627224562 and 0.6034956172774316, against published Parent values 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. The higher Child cluster retains coherent fused heteroaryl/carbonyl topology; several vinyl, alkynyl and substituent variants share 0.6359255566633433. A more disrupted carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.5157890871704487, and simple fragments remain at 0.5. The 118-heavy-atom assembly scores only 0.5663118007939372, so extensive assembly alone does not recreate the higher-score arrangement. Child size expansion is evident in 111 proposals with at least fifty heavy atoms versus 19 for the Parent, while none of the Child highest-score decile reaches that threshold. The Parent seed-0 leader instead uses a more compact N-rich carbonyl/thione fused arrangement, although it too carries reactive hypofluorite chemistry. The Child seed-2 peroxide family persists through the final row at 0.6014374553981038.

per_task.generated_character: The molecules combine halogenated aromatic surfaces with saturated amines, aminals, cyclic sulfinamides/sulfonamides or thioethers. Median size is 35 heavy atoms, range 1 to 79. Seed 0 develops a polycyclic amino/aminal scaffold attached to an aryl sulfinamide and an aryl hypohalite; seed 1 has a more compact aryl imidazolidine/aminal system; seed 2 has an azetidine/thioaryl/biphenyl family. Basic amine-like centres and hydrophobic rings are plainly available. The familiar amine/aryl motifs give these structures medicinal-chemistry recognisability, but reactive substituents, aminal stability and unresolved stereochemistry limit confidence in makeability and drug likeness.
liabilities: Aryl hypohalites occur within the highest-score family; their presence is not evidence that O-halogen reactivity is desirable for a real ligand.
Aminal centres, strained azetidine/cage motifs, sulfur oxidation-state changes and extensive aromatic halogenation create unresolved stability, geometry and physicochemical questions.
missing_features: The seed-2 leading family does not reproduce the connected amino/aminal ring arrangement of the higher Child seeds or the strongest Parent seed; more nitrogen or aromatic area alone is not justified by this contrast.

Stable, stereochemically resolved representatives of the leading amine/aryl arrangements are not established. The seed-0 leader has five unassigned tetrahedral stereocentres despite the complete absence of stereochemical annotations in the digest.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial best is 0.01904115112334333. A small N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197, whereas the more extensive amino/aryl assemblies reach Child maxima 0.9953960040791591, 0.9752746292237555 and 0.9056502535256781. The corresponding Parent maxima are 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864. The visible association is with organised amine-bearing aromatic assemblies rather than sulfonyl content or size alone: a 79-heavy-atom repeated sulfonamide structure scores 0.02886305884970262. High Child scores coexist with O-Cl/O-Br groups; 54 of its 87 highest-score molecules contain an O-halogen bond, versus none in the Parent highest-score decile. Thus the scoring gradient does not ensure chemically stable aryl substitution. Seed 2 finishes at 0.7671339307714703 within its azetidine/thioaryl family, below its own earlier maximum; no docking pose, binding mechanism or experimental activity can be inferred from these records.

per_task.generated_character: The principal family joins ethoxy/alkyl-substituted aromatic groups to N-methyl carbonyl heterocycles, often through fused, bridged or ring-expanded N-rich systems. Median size is 32 heavy atoms, range 1 to 67; halogen presence is lower here than in the other task outputs, at the digest rate 0.2207. Seed-0 leaders combine two aryl groups with an N-N-containing fused carbonyl ring; seed 1 uses an expanded heterocycle with carbonyl and ether/amine positions; seed 2 produces fused N-methyl dicarbonyl polycycles. Carbonyl/aryl building blocks are conventional, but strained fusions, N-N bonds and unusual medium-ring connectivity make overall synthesis uncertain.
liabilities: Four-membered fusions and medium-ring N-rich carbonyl systems recur among leaders, with unspecified configurations where tetrahedral stereocentres occur.

Some late variants add N-Br bonds, and graph perception flags small all-aromatic cycles in 55 proposals; those flags require geometric review rather than being treated as valid drug-like aromatic systems automatically.
missing_features: The trajectories do not show a broadly successful, simpler way to arrange the same aryl and N-methyl carbonyl features without introducing strained fusions or N-N-rich closures.

An established higher-score functional-group requirement cannot be identified from this narrow numerical range. Carbonyl groups, heteroatoms and rings are already present; their connectivity remains the visible unresolved variable.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.1678386594791329. Child maxima are 0.2423322850364201, 0.22954347803874947 and 0.2312080715343244, against Parent maxima 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313. In seed 0, the leader and closely related carbonyl/N-methyl ring variants score 0.2423322850364201, 0.2401886445446548 and 0.2369171205806659. An aromatic ether lacking this carbonyl/N-methyl arrangement scores 0.11709181070641599, while a 67-heavy-atom joined assembly scores 0.11974360856846294 and a bare carbon scores 0.0. This suggests sensitivity to the arrangement of aromatic and N-carbonyl features, without a monotone benefit from size or ring elaboration. The Parent expresses related N-methyl carbonyl-ring chemistry, with different aryl and fusion patterns. The Child seed-2 final N-brominated fused carbonyl structure scores 0.22254096353449848; a good local score does not validate its reactivity.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fluorinated N-rich fused carbonyl heterocycles, with median 27 heavy atoms and range 1 to 59. Seed 0 adds fluoropyridyl and fluorinated cyclobutene-like substituents; seed 1 develops a fused dicarbonyl scaffold with an amino group, thiol and fluorinated small unsaturated ring; seed 2 favours an expanded conjugated O/N ring carrying an acyl fluoride. These are not simple fluorinated amides: several leaders carry N-F bonds, strained small-ring fusions, or a hydrolysable acyl halide, and their synthetic plausibility is questionable.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 277 of 870 proposals and 49 of the highest-score 87; the leading seed-1 structure includes an N-fluorinated unsaturated three-membered ring alongside additional fused-ring strain.

The set contains 29 acyl halides, 85 structures with a small all-aromatic ring flag, and a low-score oversized dimer-like tail. These graph alerts are not measured reaction rates or proofs of impossibility.
missing_features: The Child does not reproduce the higher Parent seed-0 and seed-2 arrangements of saturated heterocycle, amine/imine and fluorinated substituents. This does not establish a target-specific pharmacophore or justify importing a benchmark answer.

A stable version of the compact polar fluorinated family without N-F bonds, unsaturated small-ring strain or acyl fluoride is not demonstrated at comparable scores. Stereochemical definition is also absent from the leading stereogenic structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.0020944534688323298. Child maxima are 0.5178182531715916, 0.637621765849926 and 0.44590575201147736, below corresponding Parent maxima 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813. Higher Child scores combine compact fluorinated scaffolds with N-rich carbonyl/amine functionality: the seed-1 three-membered N-F ring leader scores 0.637621765849926, while its ring-expanded final analogue scores 0.61034978472003. A 59-heavy-atom coupled analogue retaining many of those nominal groups scores 1.7258766434582876e-25, and the terminal single fluorine in seed 0 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Seed 2 changes a conjugated acyl-fluoride macrocyclic arrangement scoring 0.35632749964483745 at evaluation 299 to a more saturated N/O-containing final arrangement scoring 0.006443681365581715. Size, topology and polar-group placement matter jointly in these observations; fluorine count alone does not explain them. The Parent leaders offer alternative fluorinated amine/imine and ring arrangements, but also retain N-halogen and strained-ring liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a1818ac8ff05, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations per session with 290 optimizer proposals. Across its 4,350 proposals, structure perception flags 546 N-halogen, 241 O-halogen, 248 peroxide and 37 acyl-halide molecules; matched Parent n-cf8d309c06de counts are 888, 162, 118 and 8. Categories overlap. Some highly scored amino/aryl compounds carry O-Cl or O-Br, and compact N-rich leaders carry N-F. Lower N-halogen incidence therefore coexists with increased exposure to other reactive groups. This is an observed chemistry association, not attribution to the changed predictor.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated set does not reliably separate ordinary substituent chemistry from reactive bonds attached to heteroatoms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal system could distinguish carbon halogenation, heteroatom halogenation, peroxide formation and acyl-halide formation as chemically different edits and compare stable local alternatives using current-session feedback. Treat this as a testable feasibility capability, not an extra benchmark reward or a claim that removing every alert improves the endpoint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a1818ac8ff05 under the same frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and observation budget. Ring-closure text rates are near unity, yet the observed leaders include a densely bridged carboxamide cage, unsaturated three-membered N-F and sulfur rings, and four-membered fusions in carbonyl heterocycles. Graph perception flags small all-aromatic cycles in 185 Child proposals versus 170 for n-cf8d309c06de. These are structural warning flags, not conformational feasibility calculations. The high scores of some flagged molecules show that labels alone do not certify reasonable geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich ring construction is present, but reliably feasible ring closure and fusion geometry is not demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring edits aware of ring size, bridge connectivity, unsaturation and local geometry, and retain less strained alternatives with comparable polar/aromatic connectivity for feedback-based comparison. The missing capability is demonstrated feasible construction, not simply more rings or automatic rejection of every small ring; no component-level causal conclusion follows here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a1818ac8ff05, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and fixed session budget: 85 proposals have at most six heavy atoms and 150 have at least fifty, versus 98 and 46 in matched n-cf8d309c06de trajectories. Recorded examples include late single atoms and diatomics at the score floor, a 118-heavy-atom assembly with only modest local score, and a 59-heavy-atom coupled heterocycle with an almost zero score. Higher-score sizes differ across chemical families; the output supports examination of both tails, not a universal preference for smaller or larger molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale when generating destructive fragments or repeated large assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Monitor both fragmentation and repeated scaffold growth relative to useful structures observed in the current session, and provide edits that preserve or rebuild coherent functional-group connectivity. Compare their accepted outcomes under the same budget; do not impose a task-specific size target or infer that any fixed size cutoff is justified by this panel.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a1818ac8ff05, all frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and the same session budget. Every task digest reports charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0, while RDKit flags unassigned tetrahedral stereocentres in 2,417 of 4,350 Child proposals. The leading amine/aminal cage has five unassigned centres. These neutral strings still contain amine-like groups; absence of a charge token is not absence of basic chemistry. No measured protonation distribution or stereochemical score sensitivity is available.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurations and ionisation states are not explicitly represented in the emitted structures, even when the scaffold makes them relevant.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: If allowed by the representation contract, make configuration and chemically reasonable protonation explicit, or at least retain an ambiguity diagnostic for stereogenic and ionisable outputs. Evaluate usefulness from the current session rather than assuming that a particular configuration or charged state is rewarded. This gap concerns chemical specification, not an established explanation of endpoint loss.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-a1818ac8ff05, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and the fixed session budget. An aryl Br/F pair ties exactly at 0.42956033293511225; another fused heteroaryl series with vinyl, alkynyl and peripheral substituent changes shares 0.6359255566633433. Full proposal sets have many typed scaffolds, yet their highest-score deciles include related fused families: two such sets contain 26 typed/16 generic and 23 typed/12 generic scaffolds among 87 records. These unequal-size samples do not by themselves prove diversity collapse or identify the cause of any score difference; the matched Parent also has concentrated leader families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral analogue variation is abundant, but its score value and the value of replacing the underlying core remain unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Track which skeleton changes versus peripheral substitutions actually move observed labels, and preserve chemically distinct core alternatives while continuing to compare them using session feedback. Treat typed and generic scaffold variety as descriptive diagnostics, not a new objective or a guarantee that more scaffold diversity improves scores. The transferable observation is limited to these recorded families and conditions.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
